images.title: Sameeksha's empty floor
images.purpose: Set the scene: a 12 ft by 16 ft floor seen from above that must be covered with equal square tiles.
images.composition: One large empty rectangle (the floor seen from above) sits slightly left of centre with wide white margins; a single loose square tile with a question mark rests to its right.
exact_structure: One rectangle, the room floor seen from above, wider than tall in the ratio 16 to 12, filled very light grey with a thin dark outline (#2B2B2B), no grid lines inside it.
A grey (#6B7280) dimension line with arrowheads runs along the bottom edge, labelled 16 ft.
A grey (#6B7280) dimension line with arrowheads runs along the left edge, labelled 12 ft.
Exactly one small square tile filled teal (#0072B2) sits to the right of the rectangle, outside it, tilted slightly as if about to be placed.
A large reddish purple (#CC79A7) question mark is drawn on the loose tile.
No other objects, no furniture, no people.
rejection: any grid, tiles or division lines drawn inside the floor rectangle
more than one loose tile, or the tile drawn with a size label
the floor drawn taller than wide or with sides not in the ratio 16 to 12
images.takeaway: We need one square tile size that covers the whole 12 ft by 16 ft floor exactly.
images.description: An empty rectangular floor marked 12 ft by 16 ft with one teal square tile marked with a question mark beside it.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to guess the tile size before any calculation; the empty floor keeps the question open.

image_decisions.why: The hook needs a picture of the floor and a tile so students can imagine the tiling question.
